_what: Labels the owner has ruled on that the camera reference disagrees with. scripts/mai_camera_raw.py applies these AFTER the camera pass and the gold-passage splice, locating each turn by its words (scripts/lib_locate.py), and refuses to write if a text cannot be found or matches more than three blocks.
_why_it_exists: The camera is the best speaker evidence in this repo, but it is not the owner. When a recorded owner decision and the camera disagree, the owner decides, and their ruling has to survive every future rebuild -- an owner decision that lives only in a commit message gets destroyed later. See data/speaker_adjudications.json, ep61_farhan_restore.

ep53.why: OWNER RULING, recorded in data/speaker_adjudications.json as ep53_round2@29:59: the owner split the moment by ear into 'Okey, baik, YB.' = Haziq and 'Beria,' = Rafizi. MAI cuts it differently -- 'Hmm. Okey.' at 29:58 and 'Baik, YB.' at 30:00 -- and the camera gives both to Rafizi, because the mixer is already on him for the answer. THE ANCHOR HAS TO BE THREE TOKENS (lib_locate's MIN_TOKENS), and 'Baik, YB.' is two, so it spans both blocks and carries 'Hmm.' along with it. That is accepted rather than worked around: the owner's own text starts at 'Okey', so 'Okey.' is theirs by the ruling, and the whole thing then reads as one acknowledgement -- 'Hmm. Okey. Baik, YB.' -- which is exactly the utterance they transcribed. 'Beria, beria...' stays Rafizi, as ruled.

_split_at_words: Optional on a rule: true means the block is CUT at the rule's literal words before relabelling, so a ruling can land on part of a MAI turn that fused two speakers (ep53 2:19:14). The words and what follows them in that turn go to `who`; what precedes keeps its label; both halves keep the stamp.
